clue.text: Deprived female wearing part of army uniform

indicators.note: the beret is worn, so it sits around the letter for the female, holding it inside

parts.note: a beret is the cap worn by many soldiers

explanation.surface: A woman soldier has lost something while dressed in her service kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Bereft is a synonym for deprived, describing someone who has been robbed of something.

clue.text: Warders' complaint over Easter break

definitions.note: the possessive reads as the plural noun naming the warders themselves

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a beef is a grumble or complaint

indicators.note: the word Easter is broken up and its letters reshuffled

explanation.surface: Prison guards grumble about their spring holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' looks like the Easter holiday, but it is the anagram signal: EASTER becomes EATERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefeaters is the popular name for the Yeoman Warders of the Tower of London.

clue.text: So-shaped glass, for lots of drinks?

definitions.meaning: a glass with a circular shape, such as a bowl
a set of drinks bought for everyone in a group at once

explanation.surface: A glass of a certain shape for buying a whole party a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Round describes a circular shape and also a set of drinks bought for a group.

clue.text: Expression of disgust about head's subtle tactic

indicators.note: the exclamation goes about, or around, the word for head

parts.note: fie is an old exclamation of disgust
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: Someone sniffs in disgust at the boss's crafty manoeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' means a headland, NESS, not a person's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Finesse is delicate skill or a subtle manoeuvre, as in bridge.

clue.text: Free invention bringing cooler temperature to huge area

parts.note: a fan is something that cools you
Asia is the largest continent

explanation.surface: Somebody dreams up a scheme to make a vast region a little cooler.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantasia is a musical composition in free form, an improvised flight of invention.

clue.text: Part of church where one hears "I will"?

indicators.note: the clue words are what you hear spoken, standing for a word of the same sound

parts.note: the contraction I'll is short for I will

explanation.surface: In church the bride and groom make their vows.
explanation.walkthrough: AISLE sounds like I'LL; the wedding picture fits, as vows are said at the altar end of the aisle.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passage between pews or a side section of a church.

clue.text: Strip I would look over in paper

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for look is placed above the contraction for I would

parts.note: a tab is a small strip or tag
lo is an old word meaning look
I'd is short for I would

explanation.surface: Someone says they would examine a strip of something in the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabloid is a popular newspaper printed on smaller pages.

clue.text: Capital tree-trunk, oak

parts.note: the stock is the trunk or main stem of a tree
the holm oak is an evergreen oak, often just called holm

explanation.surface: A list of excellent types of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockholm is the capital city of Sweden.

clue.text: A borderline call attracting attention

parts.note: a hem is the edge or border of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A marginal decision gets everyone looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahem is the little cough someone gives to catch others' attention.

clue.text: Revelation that could cause one's death

definitions.meaning: making something known publicly, a disclosure
being left out unprotected in freezing weather can kill

explanation.surface: A disclosure that might prove fatal.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposure means both a disclosure and dangerous lack of shelter from the elements.

clue.text: Bovine type is into horses at special times of year

indicators.note: the ox is placed into the word for horses, cutting it open

parts.note: equines are members of the horse family
an ox is a bovine animal

explanation.surface: A cow-like creature has a fondness for horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is into' reads like 'is keen on', a bovine fond of horses, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Equinoxes are the two dates each year when day and night are of equal length.

clue.text: Mathematician has nothing to put into trunk

indicators.note: the letter for nothing is placed inside the word for a tree trunk

parts.note: a bole is the trunk of a tree
O, the round zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A mathematician has nothing to pack in his luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunk' suggests luggage; here it is the bole of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: George Boole was the English mathematician who devised Boolean algebra.

clue.text: Seen to dry docks, after disaster here?

definitions.text: Seen to dry docks, after disaster here?

indicators.note: a disaster throws things into chaos, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Ships end up stranded high and dry after coming to grief at this notorious spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of SEEN TO DRY DOCKS are rearranged; the whole clue also describes the reef as a scene of shipwrecks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eddystone Rocks are a dangerous reef off Plymouth, site of a famous lighthouse and many wrecks.

clue.text: Despairing of a husband? Book here, perhaps

definitions.meaning: an old phrase for an unmarried woman thought past the age of finding a husband
a book might be found standing on a ledge in a bookcase

explanation.surface: A lonely woman looks for comfort in reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means unlikely to marry and also literally stored on a shelf.

clue.text: Note stuck through peg for student

indicators.note: the note is pushed into the middle of the peg

parts.note: a tee is the little peg a golf ball sits on
UT is the old name for the note now called doh

explanation.surface: A musical note is pinned in place for a pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutee is a student who is taught by a tutor.

clue.text: Reprimanded and removed from list

definitions.meaning: marked with a tick as done and crossed off

explanation.surface: Someone was scolded and taken off the register.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticked off means both scolded and checked off an itemised list.

clue.text: Where Puck took lovers to be in inconsistent health

definitions.meaning: in A Midsummer Night's Dream Puck leads the lovers astray, chanting that he will lead them this way and that through the wood
someone whose health keeps changing for better and worse is said to be variable

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's sprite drags the young couples around until they feel unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes both Puck's back-and-forth leading of the lovers and fluctuating health.

clue.text: Holding two lines in error from one's stars

indicators.note: the word for in error holds the two letters inside it

parts.note: astray means wrong or in error
L stands for line, so two lines is LL

explanation.surface: An astrologer admits two lines of the forecast are wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrally means in relation to the stars, as of fate read from them.

clue.text: Dog tore on ahead, always coming back

indicators.note: the word for on is put in front of the others

parts.note: RE means on or about, as in a business letter
a cur is a mongrel dog
rent is a past tense of rend, to tear

explanation.surface: A dog ripped something and then ran off in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Something recurrent keeps happening again and again, returning repeatedly.

clue.text: I really approve book taken from southern resort

indicators.note: the letter for book is removed from the seaside town

parts.note: Brighton is a seaside resort on England's south coast

explanation.surface: A guidebook is removed from a holiday town and the reader cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIGHTON is a resort on the south coast of England; removing B leaves the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Right on is a slang exclamation of strong agreement or approval.

clue.text: Corporal beginning to push hard for beautiful girl

parts.note: Corporal Nym is a soldier in Shakespeare's Henry V and The Merry Wives of Windsor

indicators.note: only the first letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A corporal starts to push hard to win a lovely young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporal' seems a generic rank, but it means Shakespeare's Corporal Nym.
explanation.definitionFit: A nymph is a mythological maiden, and by extension any beautiful young woman.

clue.text: Formal wear for highly informal sort of party

definitions.meaning: a tie worn round the collar with a suit
a ... party is old American slang for a lynching by hanging

explanation.surface: Dress code for a very casual get-together.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is grim: a necktie party is a lynching.
explanation.definitionFit: A necktie is formal neckwear, and a necktie party is slang for a hanging.

clue.text: They try to reduce importance given to spectators

parts.note: weight means importance or influence
watchers are people who look on

explanation.surface: Onlookers are thought to matter a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Weight Watchers is the slimming organisation whose members try to lose weight.

clue.text: Child eating a second slice of this?

indicators.note: the child takes in the other letters, which go inside

parts.note: a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A youngster tucks into another piece of breakfast bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is served in slices of toast, so the definition points at the thing sliced.

clue.text: In Clare's town, endless universal tedium

indicators.note: the letter for universal is placed inside the shortened town
the last letter of the town's name is removed

parts.note: Ennis is the county town of County Clare in Ireland
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: Life in an Irish town is endlessly boring for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: ENNIS loses its last letter to give ENNI, and U goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a feeling of listless boredom or tedium.

clue.text: Seabird raising some others

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising lifts the word so it reads upwards

parts.note: auks are other seabirds, a family including puffins

explanation.surface: A seabird lifts up some of its neighbours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some others' means other seabirds: AUKS, read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A skua is a large predatory seabird that harries gulls.

clue.text: Whip has nothing to say

indicators.note: the word for nothing is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: nowt is northern English dialect for nothing

explanation.surface: A whip has nothing at all to offer.
explanation.walkthrough: KNOUT is pronounced like NOWT, the northern English word for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A knout is a Russian lash, a whip once used for flogging.

clue.text: Suddenly, everyone agreed to go round clubs

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: the word for agreed is put around the letter for clubs

parts.note: at one means in agreement
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: All of a sudden the whole group consented to visit the nightspots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' suggests nightclubs; it is the card suit, C.
explanation.definitionFit: All at once is an idiom meaning suddenly, without warning.

clue.text: Relationship any fit, if properly organised

indicators.note: the letters are put into the right order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Any match will do if it is arranged properly.
explanation.definitionFit: An affinity is a natural relationship or close connection between people or things.

clue.text: Sort of map that gives assistance

definitions.meaning: a ... map shows the height of the land by shading or contours
help given to those in need, such as aid after a disaster

explanation.surface: A kind of chart that helps people out.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief means both help for the needy and a map showing terrain heights.
